proposal.summary: 0x805a1c is CM550's fault count table: e2m 1031 DGFUCUBF 'FAULT_COUNT_TABLE.H' (1250 bytes; CM848's e2m names the same record Fault_Count_Table). It holds 125 10-byte records, one per fault code index, and lives in the flash parameter block, so the counts survive key cycles. Each record is status_change_time (dword), last_countdown_time (dword, the +4 field the e2m fault countdown uses), status (byte: bit 0 = active, bit 1 = holds a snapshot slot) and occurrence_count (byte). The layout comes from all 44 accessing instructions in 13 functions, checked against the RAM dump and both flash copies. The 27 unreferenced rows sit inside records 2-117 (10 of them in the middle of a dword) and nothing uses them. They are leftovers from the J90280.05 address map, so they go, together with the two field label rows. One user, cm550_phase2_sensor_data_processor (0x1452e), is a fall-through split of the countdown function 0x144bc and should be deleted.

fields.name: status_change_time
fields.comment: +0: key_on_hour_meter (0.2 s counts) when the fault last became active (status 3) or inactive (status 2) - cm550_processFaultScanGroup stores it (move.l at 0x14972 / 0x14bd0). The first countdown step waits until key_on_hour_meter minus it reaches the mode's elapsed time before countdown (e2m DGnnELTM at 0x80654c + 8 x mode); cm550_oldestDiagnosticTimestampSearch picks the snapshot slot whose fault has the smallest one (cmp.l at 0x146fa); cm550_resetFaultStatus zeroes it. Unsigned (sub.l then cmp.l / bls)

fields.name: last_countdown_time
fields.comment: +4: key_on_hour_meter at the last countdown step (move.l at 0x145bc); 0 until the first step - the activation (clr.l at 0x14988) and cm550_resetFaultStatus (clr.l at 0x2fe0e) zero it. While it is not 0 each step waits until key_on_hour_meter minus it reaches the mode's count down rate (e2m DGnnCUDN at 0x806550 + 8 x mode). Unsigned (sub.l then cmp.l / bhi)

fields.name: status
fields.comment: +8: bit 0 = active / bit 1 = given a snapshot slot in diagnostic_fault_code_table. cm550_processFaultScanGroup writes 3 on activation (after cm550_diagnosticCodeRegistrar assigns the slot) and 2 on deactivation (whatever bit 1 was - in the RAM dump fault 70 is 2 and holds no slot); the registrar writes 0 (from 2) or 1 (from 3) to the oldest fault whose slot it hands to a new fault; cm550_resetFaultStatus releases the slot when the status is 2 and writes 0. Readers test bit 0 (btst #0 in the countdown) or group 1 / 3 against 0 / 2 (cm550_FUN_000315be / cm550_FUN_00013ed8)

fields.name: occurrence_count
fields.comment: +9: times the fault became active: +1 on each new fault bit mapped to it up to 255 (cmpi.b #0xff / bcc at 0x1491e) and -1 per countdown step (subq.b at 0x145d4); at 0 the record is cleared and the fault leaves previously_active_dtc_list. DM1 / DM2 send it capped at 127 (cmpi.b #0x7f / bls) and the InSite fault list (J1587 PID 194 layout) sends it whole; cm550_insitePidDtcHandler skips a fault whose count is 0. Unsigned

structs.evidence: Every access, decoded by hand from the ROM (llvm-mc-18 cannot decode the CPU32 scaled-index modes): movea.l #base,a0 then (0,a0,dN.w*1 or *2) with the index = code x 10 ((x + 4x) x 2, x x 10 or moveq #10 strides). +0 (base 0x805a1c, 6 instructions): move.l 0x14564 / 0x14706, cmp.l 0x146fa, stores 0x14972 / 0x14bd0, clr.l 0x2fe04. +4 (base 0x805a20, 6 instructions; the current .cpp shows raw 0x805a20): tst.l 0x1454e / 0x14580, move.l 0x14598, store 0x145bc, clr.l 0x14988 / 0x2fe0e. +8 (base 0x805a24, 17 instructions): byte btst / tst.b / cmpi.b #1-#3 / move.b #1-#3 / clr.b / move.b. +9 (base 0x805a25, 15 instructions): byte tst.b / cmpi.b #0xff + addq.b / cmpi.b #1 + subq.b / cmpi.b #0x7f / clr.b / move.b. Total: 44 instructions in 13 functions. No ROM operand, pointer or branch reaches any other address in 0x805a1c-0x805efd. The only other reference is the parameter ID table entry (0x35524) for e2m block 1031. Count 125: cm550_FUN_000315be (0x316c0) and cm550_insitePidDtcHandler (0x14fa2) loop with cmpi.b #0x7d,d3 / bcs and a stride of 10; cm550_FUN_00014872 accepts code indexes < 0x7d; e2m length 1250 = 125 x 10; the same index addresses the 125 fault data records DG0000FU-DG0124FU (6 bytes at 0x8067c4). RAM dump: 13 records in use (e.g. record 1 = 0d8d3652 00000000 03 01, record 48 = ... 03 0b), +4 is 0 in all of them. Both flash parameter block copies in the dumped ROM (0x4a86 / 0x6a86) have the same layout with older counts. Counterpart, not twin, of CM848 fault_state_t (the 7-byte fault_state_records_cal records of the same e2m record, with a countdown step count instead of the second time), so the type name must differ.

globals.comment: e2m 1031 +0 DGFUCUBF 'FAULT_COUNT_TABLE.H' (1250 bytes = 125 x 10; CM848's e2m names the record Fault_Count_Table): one fault_count_record_t per fault code index 0-124. The index is that of the fault's 6-byte fault data record (e2m DG0000FU-DG0124FU at 0x8067c4), and the fault code assignment table DGFUCATB (0x80656c) maps each status bit to it (125 = none). Every access is 0x805a1c / 0x805a20 / 0x805a24 / 0x805a25 + index x 10 (44 instructions in 13 functions); cm550_FUN_000315be and cm550_insitePidDtcHandler walk all 125 (cmpi.b #0x7d with a stride of 10). Writers: cm550_processFaultScanGroup (activation / deactivation), cm550_countDownPreviouslyActiveFault (countdown), cm550_diagnosticCodeRegistrar (snapshot slot hand-over), cm550_resetFaultStatus (clear). Readers: the datalogger fault-code triggers cm550_FUN_00013cc8 / cm550_FUN_00013e64 / cm550_FUN_00013ed8, cm550_oldestDiagnosticTimestampSearch, the trending task cm550_FUN_000315be (any fault active), cm550_insitePidDtcHandler, cm550_insiteFaultDetailBuilder, j1939HandlePgn65226Dm1ActiveDtc and cm550_previousDtcListBuilder (DM2). The 10 bytes after it (0x805efe) are not a record: no code reaches them, because the empty snapshot slot code 125 is never used as an index, and they hold the same constant in RAM and both flash blocks. No _cal: it is in the flash parameter block (RAM 0x804f9a-0x806547). cm550_loadParameterBlock1FromFlash / 2 load the block at start-up and cm550_saveParameterBlock1ToFlash / 2 save it at power-down, and the dumped ROM holds copies at flash 0x4a86 / 0x6a86. Counterpart of CM848 fault_state_records_cal (fault_state_t[170]: 7-byte records with a countdown step count in place of the second time). (were diagnostic_fault_status_change_time at +0 / diagnostic_fault_status_table at +8 / diagnostic_fault_occurrence_count at +9, and 27 unreferenced rows from the J90280.05 address map: diagnostic_fault_status_array at +26 / diagnostic_snapshot_throttle_value at +28 / diagnostic_snapshot_fuel_value at +34 / diagnostic_snapshot_sensor_reading at +38 / diagnostic_snapshot_throttle_raw at +40 / fault_flags_active_base at +982 / fault_status_flags_2 at +984 / engine_fault_status_reg at +986 / io_fault_status_reg_1 at +990 / io_fault_status_reg_2 at +992 / io_fault_status_reg_3 at +994 / io_fault_status_reg_4 at +996 / vp44_status_register_5e12 at +1014 / vp44_fault_status_reg at +1016 / vp44_fso_fault_flags_active at +1018 / fault_flags_history_base at +1046 / fault_status_flags_8_previous at +1048 / engine_fault_latch_reg at +1050 / io_fault_latch_reg_1 at +1054 / io_fault_latch_reg_2 at +1056 / io_fault_latch_reg_3 at +1058 / io_fault_latch_reg_4 at +1060 / vp44_fso_fault_flags at +1078 / vp44_fso_fault_accumulator at +1080 / vp44_fso_fault_flags_history at +1082 / diagnostic_fault_group_bitmask_array at +1110 / rpm_histogram_buffer_start at +1176; PR #53 round 91)
globals.evidence: e2m_block_addresses.py --firmware cm550 1031: block 1031 +0 DGFUCUBF (type B, 1250 bytes) resolves to 0x805a1c, and no other e2m record resolves between 0x8058d4 and 0x805f08. functions.plate_comment: Counts down one previously active fault (code_index) - the e2m fault countdown. It acts only while fault_count_table[code_index].status bit 0 is clear (btst #0) and both the fault's countdown mode (byte +5 of its 6-byte fault data record at 0x8067c4 - e2m DG0000FU) and its occurrence_count are not 0. The first step waits until key_on_hour_meter - status_change_time reaches the mode's elapsed time before countdown (e2m DGnnELTM at 0x80654c + 8 x mode: 11 h for mode 1 in this dump). Each later step waits until key_on_hour_meter - last_countdown_time reaches the mode's count down rate (DGnnCUDN at 0x806550 + 8 x mode: 4 h). A step stores key_on_hour_meter in last_countdown_time and takes 1 off occurrence_count. At 0 it clears the record (cm550_resetFaultStatus) and moves the last previously_active_dtc_list entry into the fault's place (with its J1587 count). Nothing in it debounces. Counterpart of CM848 cm848_faultTimeoutHandler (0x1c9a0): the same e2m settings with a step count in place of the second time (was cm550_diagnosticCodeDebounceHandler; PR #53 round 91)
functions.evidence: Disassembly 0x144bc-0x1466e. a3 = 0x8067c4 (fault data records), a5 = &key_on_hour_meter, a4 = &_inactive_fault_debounce_scan_index. 0x144e6 btst #0 on the status. 0x144fa tst.b (5,a3,index*6) reads the countdown mode. 0x14512 tst.b on occurrence_count. 0x1452e-0x1453a: a2 = 0x80654c + mode x 8, d3 = (a2), d5 = 4(a2). 0x14564 / 0x1456e: key_on - status_change_time compared with d3 (bls). 0x14598 / 0x145a2: key_on - last_countdown_time compared with d5 (bhi). 0x145bc stores key_on. 0x145d4 subq.b #1. 0x145ec jsr 0x2fddc at 0. e2m block F: DGnnELTM 'ELAPSED TIME BEFORE STARTING COUNTDOWN FOR A MODE n FAULT' at +8n, DGnnCUDN 'TIME THAT MUST ELAPSE BEFORE THE FAULT COUNT IS DECREMENTED' at +8n+4. Parameter ID 15 = 0x80654c. RAM dump: mode 1 = 198000 / 72000 counts (113 of the 125 faults use mode 1, the other 12 mode 0). CM848 cm848_faultTimeoutHandler does the same job with fault_countdown_elapsed_time_mode_0 / fault_countdown_decrement_interval_mode_0 and a 7-byte record, so the two are counterparts.

functions.plate_comment: Runs cm550_countDownPreviouslyActiveFault on each entry of previously_active_dtc_list (1 to the count in entry 0), with _inactive_fault_debounce_scan_index as the cursor. The callee moves the last entry into a cleared fault's place and steps the cursor back. cm550_faultFlagScannerAndProcessor calls it when key_on_hour_meter has moved more than 24 counts (about 5 s) since _DAT_0080052e. Counterpart of CM848 cm848_activeFaultScanProcessor (0x1cd1c) (was cm550_FUN_00014670; PR #53 round 91)
functions.evidence: Decompile line 9343: for cursor = 1 .. previously_active_dtc_list[0] calls 0x144bc with previously_active_dtc_list[cursor]; its only caller, cm550_faultFlagScannerAndProcessor (jsr at 0x14f30), runs it when 0x18 < key_on_hour_meter - _DAT_0080052e. CM848 0x1cd1c walks previously_active_dtc_list_cal the same way with an extra fault_definition_table flag test, so the two are counterparts.

functions.plate_comment: Processes one 16-fault status word per call (_fault_status_word_scan_index; cm550_faultFlagScannerAndProcessor picks the next word with a bit to process). Each bit of status word | first-occurrence word (the latter is then cleared) is compared with the previous pass's word (0x806080 + 2 x word) and gated by fault_confirm_status_word (0x806abc + 2 x word). The fault code assignment table (e2m DGFUCATB at 0x80656c) maps the bit to a fault code index (125 = none). A new bit, while active_dtc_list is not full, adds 1 to fault_count_table[index].occurrence_count (up to 255). If the fault's active-bit count at 0x80599e + index was 0, the fault also gets a snapshot slot (cm550_diagnosticCodeRegistrar), status 3, status_change_time = key_on_hour_meter and last_countdown_time = 0, and it moves from previously_active_dtc_list to active_dtc_list with its J1587 / InSite counts. A cleared bit takes 1 off the active-bit count. At 0 the fault gets status 2 and a new status_change_time and moves to previously_active_dtc_list (at most 31 entries). The function ends by storing the combined word as the next previous word. Counterpart of CM848 cm848_processFaultScanGroup (0x1d224) (was cm550_FUN_00014872; PR #53 round 91)
functions.evidence: Decompile lines 9470-9640 and the disassembly: addq.b #1 on occurrence_count after cmpi.b #0xff at 0x1491e / 0x14934; move.b #3 status at 0x1495e; move.l key_on_hour_meter to +0 at 0x14972; clr.l +4 at 0x14988; move.b #2 at 0x14bbc and move.l key_on to +0 at 0x14bd0; code index from (local_6 + word x 16) x 2 + 0x80656c (e2m block F +0x20 DGFUCATB 'FAULT CODE ASSIGNMENT TABLE', 600 bytes) checked < 0x7d. cross_firmware_matches.csv already pairs 0x14872 with CM848 0x1d224 (score 21). CM848's version adds OBD steps (cm848_latchNewlyActiveFault, fault_handled_bitmap) and uses the 7-byte record, so the two are counterparts with the same stem.

functions.plate_comment: Clears fault_count_table[code_index]: occurrence_count, status_change_time and last_countdown_time = 0. When the status is 2 it then releases the fault's snapshot slot (cm550_FUN_0002fd90 writes 125 to the slot's code words at 0x80426e / 0x80462e + 48 x slot). Last, status = 0. Called by cm550_countDownPreviouslyActiveFault when the count reaches 0 and by cm550_FUN_00014812 for every previously active fault on a clear request. Counterpart of CM848 cm848_resetFaultStatus (0x1dee0) (was cm550_diagnosticTableEntryClear; PR #53 round 91)
functions.evidence: Disassembly: clr.b +9 at 0x2fdfa, clr.l +0 at 0x2fe04, clr.l +4 at 0x2fe0e, cmpi.b #2 on +8 at 0x2fe18 then bsr 0x2fd90, clr.b +8 at 0x2fe2e. references_to.py: called from 0x145ec and 0x14838. CM848 0x1dee0 clears timer / timestamp / debounce_count, runs cm848_updateFaultEntryCounters when the status is 2 (or the OBD handler is on) and writes status 0: the same role with different code, so the CM550 name takes the same stem.

functions.plate_comment: Counts down one previously active fault (param_1) - the e2m fault countdown. It acts while fault_state_records_cal[param_1].status bit 0 is clear and both the fault's countdown mode (fault_definition_table[].aging_flags & 3) and .timer are not 0. .timer is the occurrence count: cm848_processFaultScanGroup adds 1 per activation up to 255 and DM1 / DM2 cap it at 127. The first step comes when key_on_hour_meter - .timestamp exceeds the mode's Fault_Countdown_Elapsed_Time (fault_countdown_elapsed_time_mode_0 + 8 x mode). Step n + 1 comes when that difference exceeds the elapsed time + n x the mode's Count_Down_Rate (n = .debounce_count - the steps taken; the activation zeroes it). A step adds 1 to .debounce_count and takes 1 off .timer. At 0 it resets the fault (cm848_resetFaultStatus) and removes it from previously_active_dtc_list_cal. Counterpart of CM550 cm550_countDownPreviouslyActiveFault (0x144bc: a second time stamp in place of the step count) (was cm848_faultTimeoutHandler; PR #53 round 91)
functions.evidence: cm848_rom.ghidra.cpp lines 19627-19670: the compares against (&fault_countdown_elapsed_time_mode_0)[mode x 2] / (&fault_countdown_decrement_interval_mode_0)[mode x 2], the e2m Fault_Countdown_Elapsed_Time_Mode_n / Fault_Countdown_Count_Down_Rate_Mode_n (block 0023, resolved to 0x5983a / 0x5983e). Line 20092 adds 1 to .timer (up to 0xff), line 20099 zeroes .debounce_count on activation, lines 25602 / 25703 / 25807 cap .timer at 0x7f. Nothing in it times out. Optional for S1: it keeps the counterpart stems aligned with the CM550 rename.

functions.plate_comment: Runs cm848_countDownPreviouslyActiveFault on each fault of previously_active_dtc_list_cal (active_fault_scan_counter is the cursor) whose fault_definition_table entry has entry_flags bit 0 clear or aging_flags bit 7 set. The old name read it as an active fault scan, but it walks the previously active list. Counterpart of CM550 cm550_countDownPreviouslyActiveFaults (0x14670) (was cm848_activeFaultScanProcessor; PR #53 round 91)
functions.evidence: cm848_rom.ghidra.cpp lines 19736-19756: the do-while over previously_active_dtc_list_cal.slots calling cm848_faultTimeoutHandler. Optional for S1: it keeps the counterpart stems aligned.

rows_to_remove.name: cm550_phase2_sensor_data_processor
rows_to_remove.reason: function_renames.csv row, not a global: 0x1452e is not a function entry. It is the movea.l #0x80654c,a0 at byte 0x72 of 0x144bc, reached only by fall-through from the lsl.w #3,d0 at 0x1452c. references_to.py finds 0 references, and no pointer 0x0001452e is in the ROM or the RAM / extended RAM / EEPROM dumps. The row came from the J90280.05 relocation map (phase2_sensor_data_processor 0x11060 -> 0x1452e). Its unaff_D2b / A3 / A4 / A5 pseudo-parameters are the registers 0x144bc loads, and 0x144bc already decompiles the same code.

proposal.notes:
Pointer locals / parameters: none. Every access reloads an absolute field address (movea.l #0x805a1c / 0x805a20 / 0x805a24 / 0x805a25) plus an index register. The a2 / a3 pointers in the users walk the 6-byte fault data records at 0x8067c4 or the countdown modes at 0x80654c, not this table. code_index / fault_status stay ushort (indexes and values). The unaff_ pseudo-parameters go away with the 0x1452e split.

The 27 rows are not a different structure. No ROM operand reaches any of their addresses, they fall inside records 2-117 (10 of them in the middle of a dword), and the RAM dump and both flash copies show fault records there. The real status / first-occurrence / previous words are at 0x806000 / 0x806040 / 0x806080. The rows arrived in commit 1d82e3f4 (J90280.05 removal), and the relocation map is also where the 0x1452e function row came from. The type-only templates fault_status_registers_t and vp44_fault_state_t (structure_definitions.csv) mirror the stale rows at 0x805df2-0x805e00 / 0x805e14-0x805e16. They have no instance and no user (0 .cpp hits; only firmware_types.hpp), so they can be removed too (optional, header-only change).

Applying:
(1) Add the 4 fault_count_record_t rows as a type-only template (empty address column; comments are comma-free).
(2) Retype and rename the 0x805a1c row.
(3) Remove the 29 global rows.

verdicts.reason: I decoded every access again with capstone (CM550 mode; I read the index scale from the operand detail because the text output drops *2 on .l indexes). I also scanned every byte offset of the ROM: the only 32-bit values in 0x805a1c-0x805f07 are the four field bases, at 44 code sites, plus the parameter ID table entry 0x35524 / 0x35528. A displacement sweep of all 755 functions found no base+disp access into the range, and a sanity test found the known 0x8067c4+disp accesses. The fields: +0 is a long, 6 sites (move.l 0x14564 / 0x14706, cmp.l 0x146fa, store key_on 0x14972 / 0x14bd0, clr.l 0x2fe04). +4 is a long, 6 sites (tst.l 0x1454e / 0x14580, move.l 0x14598, store key_on 0x145bc, clr.l 0x14988 / 0x2fe0e). +8 is a byte, 17 sites. +9 is a byte, 15 sites. No access touches +1..+3 or +5..+7 alone, and none reads +8/+9 as a word. Every index register holds code x 10: (x + 4x) with a *2 scale, x*4+x+x, or a stride of moveq #10. Both dwords are unsigned (sub.l, then cmp.l with bls / bhi; 0x146fa cmp.l with bls). The count is unsigned (cmpi.b #$ff with bcc at 0x1491e; cmpi.b #$7f with bls at 0x32348 / 0x324b6). Roles: +4 is key_on at the last countdown step and gates the later steps against DGnnCUDN at 4(a2), a2 = 0x80654c + 8 x mode. +0 is the activation / deactivation time and gates the first step against DGnnELTM. Status values 0/1/2/3 are written at 0x147c0 / 0x14806 / 0x14bbc / 0x1495e and 0x2fe2e. The RAM dump and both flash copies (0x4a86 / 0x6a86) agree: 13 records in use and +4 = 0 in each of them. The field sizes sum to 10. All four comments are comma-free and match the code. Counterpart, not twin: CM848 fault_state_t is a 7-byte record, with .timer as the occurrence count and .debounce_count as the step count. So a separate type name is right, and data types carry no cm550_ prefix in this repository.

fault_count_table, fault_count_record_t[125]. e2m 1031 +0 DGFUCUBF is type B, 1250 bytes = 125 x 10. CM848's e2m (CHR_CC 11.10 / 11.12) names block 1031 +0 Fault_Count_Table 'FAULT_COUNT_TABLE.H'. The 125 bound appears four ways. Loops with cmpi.b #$7d and bcs at 0x316c0 (stride 10, status 1 / 3), 0x14fa2 (stride 10, count) and 0x13ebe (the 125 fault data records). Range checks cmpi.w #$7d with bcc at 0x148d8 / 0x14b6e. The fault data records DG0000FU-DG0124FU at F+0x278, 6 bytes each, 0x8067c4. The writer and reader lists match the 13 functions. The comment's claim that index 125 is never used holds. 0x146b4 has no < 0x7d test, but its only two references are the registrar's bsr at 0x14788 / 0x147ce, after the loop at 0x1475c has returned on any slot code 0x7d. Every other index source is bounded: the DGFUCATB checks, the lists filled from them, and the datalogger index bytes 0x800366+i, which only 0x13ea4 writes, with d2 < 0x7d. 0x805efe-0x805f07 holds 00080f00140025801e00 in RAM and in both flash copies, and no operand reaches it. No _cal is right: the loader 0x10e80 copies flash 0x4000 to 0x804f96 (one long), then flash 0x4004.. to RAM 0x804f9a-0x806547, so the table is flash 0x4a86 / 0x6a86 and lies outside the EEPROM mirror. The CM550 CSVs have no name collision. One evidence nit, not in the comment so nothing changes: 'no other e2m record resolves between 0x8058d4 and 0x805f08' is wrong as written. Block 1097 DGAEFUBF / DGIEFUBF / DGAEFOBF / DGIEFOBF / JCFUCUDA resolve to 0x8058d4-0x805a1b. The true statement is that JCFUCUDA (1097 +0xC0, 136 bytes) ends at 0x805a1b, no record resolves in 0x805a1c-0x805f07 apart from DGFUCUBF, and 1329 SSPWCU at 0x805f08 comes next.

The name cm550_countDownPreviously­ActiveFault is right. The only caller is the bsr at 0x14690 in 0x14670's walk of previously_active_dtc_list. Each step adds 1 to .debounce_count at +4 and takes 1 off .timer at +6, and at 0 calls bl 0x1dee0.
